Technologies adopted and chain description

    A CCS value chain comprises several elements within an upstream
boundary at one or multiple stationary emitters of CO2 and the down-
stream boundary at the ﬁnal sink, which could be one or multiple CO2
storage sites. This paper considers the CCS chain’s conditioning, trans-
port, intermediate storage, and injection and geological storage ele-
ments, as illustrated in Fig. 1.
    The capture of CO2 consists of all technologies and chemical pro-
cesses used to separate CO2 before or after combustion processes and
those chemical processes with an output stream gas composed mainly
of CO2 (e.g., fermentation of biomass). The conditioning element com-
prises the compression or liquefaction of CO2 , aiming to increase its den-
sity for eﬃcient transportation. The CO2 conditioning element is linked
to the transport mode adopted. If transported by pipelines, CO2 can be
compressed to higher pressures than 7.3 MPa (i.e., dense phase ﬂuid). If
